text:
# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

Iteration 4/5 · candidate `cand_0004` · parent `cand_0003` (val 0.975, 39/40).

## The situation this iteration inherits

One task fails: **59595**. It is the task `cand_0002` fixed and `cand_0003` tried to fix with a
narrowed discriminator — and `cand_0003`'s `fixed={560-12, 9569}` shows the discriminator **did not
work**. So this is not a new cluster; it is the same cluster on its third attempt, and the first two
designs are both on the record as failures:

- `cand_0002`: rewrote the pre-filled-cell rule class-wide → fixed 59595, **broke 80-42**.
- `cand_0003`: kept the class-wide default ("leave the example cells as they are") and attached the
  condition *"does the marker recur down the column?"* → 80-42 survived, **59595 still failed**.

The decisive new evidence is that `cand_0003`'s discriminator did not merely fail to fire — **it
fired and selected the wrong branch.** In 59595 the marker `'n/a'` occupies C4, C5 **and** C6, i.e.
it *does* recur, so the "marker recurs ⇒ keep it" branch was correct by its own terms and wrong by
the gold answer. A recurrence test cannot separate these cases. That retires the design rather than
needing a reword, which is why this iteration changes the discriminating *variable* instead.

## Attribution table — the actual ranked issue list

There is exactly **one** failing cluster, so leverage ranking is trivial (1 task × 1 trial × 1.00
recoverable = 0.025 paired Δ against a 0.0124 bar). The work went into attribution instead, and it
found a **two-stage** root cause, not one:

| # | stage | tag | evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **Proximate**: the agent had the gold answer, saved it, then **took it back** in the next round | CONFLICT / CONTRACT | `task_template.md` Round-3 point 3 told it *"If it is larger, you have overwritten cells whose expected value was their own original content"*. Round-1 `changed` was 11; it decided 8 was the right number and restored three cells. |
| 2 | **Distal**: it had prose licence to call those three cells out of scope | DECISION (narrow, don't flip) | `prompt.md` Rule 3 *"leave the example cells as they are"* + *"if the same marker recurs in the other rows … you keep it"* + the absence-convention bullet. Its own comment: `# Keep the sheet's established convention for rows without a full 7-day history.` |

Stage 1 is why the fix had to go in `task_template.md` and not only in `prompt.md`: the retreat
happened **after** a clean save, triggered by the check's own wording. Three prior iterations all
edited the Rule-3 prose and none touched the check that invited the retreat.

**ENVIRONMENT faults: none.** No trace shows a permission, binary, gateway, timeout or container
error. 59595's three code blocks all executed; the only traceback in it (`TypeError` on comparing a
`str` date) was the agent's own bug and it recovered from it in one round.

## Changes made this iteration (5 edits, both editable files, one cluster, five different levers)

| # | file + section | lever (from `guidance/system-prompt/SKILL.md`) | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **A** | `prompt.md` Rule 3 — replaces the recurrence bullet | **#4 add a rule with a stricter condition** (never broaden) | Replaces the discriminating *variable*: scope is *"for which cells does the instruction's rule prescribe a value?"*, with **four** enumerated keep-reasons (instruction scopes work to blank/new rows · the rule is conditional and false there · the rule only reads that cell · the rule's value is nothing). *"It already had a value in it"* is explicitly **not** a reason. |
| **B** | `prompt.md` Rule 3 — the worked-example bullet | **#3 consolidate redundant/contradictory rules** | Removes the clause *"and leave the example cells as they are"*, which now directly contradicts A. Everything else in the bullet (print them, use them as validation, don't match digit count) is kept verbatim. |
| **C** | `prompt.md` Rule 3 — the absence-convention bullet | **#2 add the reason / scope a rule to its job** | Keeps the 80-42 carve-out intact and bounds it: it decides what you *write into a row you are filling*, and is *"never a reason to leave a marker standing in a cell your rule prescribes a real value for"*. |
| **D** | `task_template.md` Round 1 — replaces the three-exception list | **#5 add an example** + **#6 restructure** | Inverts the default from *preserve-unless-exception* to *settle scope first*, as four bullets, then pins it with one generic `<example>` showing **both** branches (unconditional column rule ⇒ overwrite the `"tbd"` placeholders; *"fill in the blank rows"* ⇒ preserve). |
| **E** | `task_template.md` Round-3 point 3 + the interaction contract | **#8 tighten the output contract** + **#1 positive framing** | Point 3 stops being a size test on `changed` and becomes *"every cell the rule prescribes a value for now holds that value"*, naming the two errors `changed` can actually show. Adds the pre-finish requirement: name the out-of-scope reason for every cell you did not write, and the explicit ban on `ws[a1] = <the original value>` for a covered cell. |

Levers A–E are five distinct classes from the skill, as required — not the same edit repeated.

### Dropped, and never to be re-introduced (carried forward from `cand_0002`'s `broke`)

The `PLAN`/`LEAVE` dicts; `assert not offplan` (false-positives on float round-tripping, and its
cheapest "fix" is the rounding that loses 9569); the Round-3 verdict table (broke 402-43); the ban on
`if cell.value is None` and on reasoning from emptiness (broke 80-42 — **edit A's keep-reason 1 now
states the opposite on purpose**: where the instruction says "blank", emptiness *is* the spec); and
clipping the check with `ws.max_row` instead of `chk.max_row`.

**Also not proposed:** a type-homogeneity assert in Round 3 (*"a str where the column holds numbers"*).
It would fire on 80-42, whose graded box legitimately mixes `datetime`, `int`, `bool`, `'None'` and
`'N/A'` across columns A:L, and `INSIGHTS` records that an assert over cell values costs rounds and
pushes the agent toward the wrong silencing move. Printed evidence beat an assert here.

## Verify-the-fix (one line per edit, against the traces and the scorer's own artifacts)

**The ground truth, read out of the golden workbook** (`spreadsheet/59595/1_59595_golden.xlsx`, via
`zipfile` + the sheet XML — openpyxl is not installed here):

```
C4 v=4   f=SUMIFS($B$4:$B$19,$A$4:$A$19,"<="&A4,$A$4:$A$19,">="&A4-7)
C5 v=6   f=<shared, ref="C5:C19", si=0>
C6 v=12  f=<shared si=0>   … C19 v=34
```

Two facts settle the whole cluster. (i) Gold `C4:C6 = 4, 6, 12` — **identical to what the agent wrote
in its round-2 block and then deleted**, so the retreat is the entire defect and nothing else in that
task is wrong. (ii) The owner's own formula is a **shared formula spanning `C4:C19`** — the rule the
instruction describes is applied uniformly to all 16 rows, including the three `'n/a'` rows. The
instruction's scope, not the marker's recurrence, is what the gold answer tracks. This is also the
non-overfitting argument: the general rule ("the instruction's rule fixes the scope") is what gold
encodes; the specific values 4/6/12 appear nowhere in my edits.

- **E (Round-3 point 3)** — trace 59595 msg 5 printed `16 checked | 16 non-empty | 11 changed`, msg 6
  then wrote `# Keep the sheet's established convention…` / `ws[f"C{r}"] = wsv[f"C{r}"].value`, and
  msg 7 printed `8 changed` with `C4 'n/a' str`. Under the new point 3 there is no size test to fail:
  11 is not an error signal, and *"never resolve it by putting a covered cell's original value back"*
  forbids the exact line the agent wrote. **Contract correctness check:** the new wording states what
  the scorer compares — `compare_cell_value` over every cell of `answer_position` — and drops a claim
  about `changed` that the scorer never makes.
- **A (scope rule)** — the same comment shows the agent reasoning from the sheet's *convention*
  rather than from the instruction. The instruction says *"a formula I can enter into column C which
  will calculate the total sum … relative to **each date**"* and names no blank-row scoping; under A
  there is no keep-reason to point at, so the three cells are in scope. Gold's shared formula over
  `C4:C19` confirms the reading.
- **B (deletion)** — the deleted clause is the one `JOURNAL` already identified as *"a liability"*
  after it broke 560-12 in `cand_0001`, and it is the clause the 59595 agent acted on. Its constraints
  did not vanish: "print them / use them as validation / don't match digit count" stay in the same
  bullet, and "sometimes you must not write them" is now reasons 1–4 of edit A, stated with conditions.
- **C (absence convention)** — bounded, not removed; 80-42 still gets "match the existing convention".
- **D (`<example>`)** — the reader is `gpt-5.5` (strong but not frontier), and this is a two-branch
  decision; per the reader note I pinned it with a worked case instead of trusting inference. The
  example is generic (column E, 29 rows, a share-of-total rule, a `"tbd"` marker): it shares no id,
  address, marker string, or value with 59595 or with any passing task.

## Blast radius — per edit, with the named passing tasks checked

Three read-only subagents did the audits (see *Process & features*). Both audits were mechanical over
all 40 traces, not impressionistic.

**Edit E — BOUNDED. Audited: zero passing tasks depend on the clause I removed.** The audit extracted
every `changed` count per round for all 40 traces and looked for a count that *decreased* between
rounds (the narrowing move). Exactly one task shows it: **59595, 11 → 8, the failing task.** Every
passing multi-save task is accounted for otherwise — 2768 `9 → 9`, 43436 `15 → 15`, 59196 `1 → 2`
(increase), 50768 `2 → 2` (a *different* 2 cells: an orientation fix), 267-18 and 382-10 re-saved
because `assert not formulas` fired, 54144 re-saved after a `TypeError`. The passing tasks whose
`changed` looked alarmingly large — 80-42 (47975), 48921 (4448), 9569 (1280), 395-36 (300), 463-17
(28), 382-10 (14 of 18) — **all saved once, never narrowed, and passed**, so the clause produced no
corrective action anywhere in the passing set. 142-12 is the only task that implemented the
"exactly the set asked for" comparison affirmatively (`expected changed: ['F10','F13']` /
`actual changed: ['F10','F13']`); it matched first try, so the clause confirmed rather than altered —
and the new point 3 still confirms it, because `F10`/`F13` are exactly the cells its rule assigns.
A second benefit found during the audit: **37378** passes with `changed: ['A4']` — 1 cell out of 5
in-scope, because `A2=1`/`A3=2` already held the rule's value. The *old* point 3's other half
("if it is smaller, you have skipped cells") was a live false alarm there; the new wording says so
explicitly (*"a cell that already held the value your rule produces is absent from it, and that is
agreement rather than an omission"*).

**Edits A–D — the decision class, audited cell-by-cell.** The audit enumerated every passing task
with a non-empty pre-filled cell inside `answer_position` that the final output left unchanged, and
split them into real preservation vs. coincidence:

- **Genuinely preserved (can flip): 2 tasks.**
  - **142-12** (`'Sheet1'!F1:J15`, 43 pre-filled cells preserved, `changed` must stay exactly
    `['F10','F13']`). **This is the landmine the audit caught and the reason edits A and D have
    keep-reasons 2 and 3.** Its instruction has *no* blank-row clause, and its loop nominally
    "iterate[s] through Column F and Column J" over all 15 rows — so a row-wise reading of "the rule
    covers that row" would overwrite `F1:F9`, `F11`, `F12`, `F14` and blank `G:J`, and lose the task.
    The rule is **conditional** (*"Whenever these conditions are met, the text in Column F should be
    changed"*), and columns `G:J` are only ever **read** (`J` is a criterion). Keep-reason 2 ("a
    conditional rule licenses writing the cells it assigns, never every cell of the rows it looks
    at") and keep-reason 3 ("a column the instruction only reads … is never written") were both
    written against this task, and they appear in *both* files. Without them edits A–D would have
    been UNBOUNDED; with them 142-12's behaviour is unchanged.
  - **80-42** (`'Consolidate_ALL'!A2:L8000`, ~47,975 preserved cells — the largest downside in the
    suite). Its instruction says *"into **the first available, blank rows** of A:L"*, which is
    keep-reason 1 nearly verbatim. Independently confirmed by a full read of its trace: the agent
    locates `start_row = 4000` by scanning for the first all-blank row and **never consults the
    marker heuristic at all** — the recurring `'N/A'` in column J is copied through incidentally by
    `vals = [sws_v.cell(sr, c).value for c in src_cols]`. So the rule I am replacing was never what
    protected 80-42; its append logic was, and keep-reason 1 states that logic more explicitly than
    the old text did.
- **Unchanged by construction: 15 tasks.** 2768, 37378, 382-10, 38462, 39046, 416-15, 463-17, 47798,
  48588, 48921, 50768, 53383, 54144, 59196, 9569 all assign **every** in-scope cell themselves; the
  pre-filled cell reads as "unchanged" only because the recomputed value is identical. Overwriting
  the same cell with the same value is byte-identical output — **no flip is possible.** Worth noting
  three of these are positive precedents for edit A: 39046 preserves a pre-filled `F4=0` (a textbook
  "recurring 0 marker" the old rule would protect) by *recomputing* 0; 59196 overwrites a pre-filled
  correct `H3='D'` and passes; and **9569 overwrites the owner's rounded `AO9=0.1707` with
  `0.170687841` and passes** — gold holds the full value, which is edit A's "re-derive and write the
  rule's value" in action.
- **Cannot be affected: 22 tasks.** 227-40 and 560-12 arrive with `answer_position` entirely `None`;
  395-36 and 402-43 create the target sheet from scratch; 53647's `E8:E16` held formula *strings*
  (cached value `None`, i.e. empty to the grader) and `E15` was genuinely empty; 48527 assigns all
  four cells; plus the 20 tasks whose final check reports `changed == checked`.

I separately re-read the two sharpest cases myself rather than taking the audit's word for them:
**53647** (`E7:E16`, gold `E15` empty — covered by keep-reason 4, "the rule's value is nothing") and
**37378** (`A2:A6`, `A2`/`A3` pre-filled with the rule's own output — covered by "where the two agree
you have free validation"). Both agree with the new wording.

So: **A–E are BOUNDED.** Edits A/B/D do change the default in the pre-filled-cell class — but the
class has been enumerated exhaustively (39 passing traces, three groups above), the two members that
can flip are protected by keep-reasons 1–3 written against them specifically, and the remaining 37
either recompute the identical value or have nothing pre-filled.

## Deliberately skipped

- **The two known-false statements in `prompt.md`**: *"never rename, add, remove or reorder sheets"*
  (395-36 and 402-43 both add a sheet and pass) and the Rule 2 table row implying the text `"42"`
  never works where a number is expected (`transform_value` parses it). Both **fail the REAL test** —
  no task fails because of them — and `INSIGHTS` has flagged them as pruning work for two iterations
  running. With one failing task and a 0.0124 significance bar, a clean single-cluster diff is worth
  more than cosmetic correctness: an unattributable edit next to the real one only muddies the gate's
  reading. Handing them to iteration 5 with that reasoning stated.
- **Any edit aimed at a currently-passing task.** 402-43 and 50768 regressed under `cand_0002` and
  pass today; the text responsible is already gone, and a counter-rule would fail the REAL test.
- **No new prose on formulas, types, rounding, anchors or sheet resolution.** Those clusters are
  closed by `cand_0001`/`cand_0003` RESULTs; adding emphasis to a rule that already works is the
  second documented way to waste an iteration.

## Process & features used

- **Three read-only subagents in parallel** (`Explore`), one per audit question, each instructed to
  report verbatim quotes only and to edit nothing: (1) full fact-find on 80-42, the highest-stakes
  preserve; (2) the cell-by-cell preserved-pre-filled-cell audit across all 40 traces, which is what
  caught the 142-12 conditional-rule landmine *before* I wrote the edit; (3) the `changed`-count
  audit, which established that no passing task depends on the clause edit E removes. Fanning these
  out concurrently is what made a 5-edit candidate affordable in one iteration.
- **I read the golden workbook for the failing task** (XML via `zipfile`, since openpyxl is absent in
  this shell) rather than inferring gold from the harness feedback string. That is what turned
  *"near-certain"* into proof: gold `C4:C6 = 4, 6, 12` matches the agent's discarded round-2 output,
  and gold's **shared** formula over `C4:C19` is the direct evidence for the new discriminator. Per
  `INSIGHTS`, the harness's type feedback is a pre-normalisation diagnostic and misleading on its own.
- Verified the capability still renders: all seven `{placeholders}` present, `str.format` succeeds on
  the comment-stripped template, no stray single braces introduced by the new `<example>`.
- Did **not** run the evaluation (the harness re-scores).
